newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sick Thai firm One Holding needs credit lifeline.
newsitem.headline: Sick Thai firm One Holding needs credit lifeline.

text.p: Ailing Thai firm One Holding Plc, the investment arm of Thailand's One group of companies, must ask creditors to extend credit lines if the company is to survive, its financial advisers said on Friday.

One Holding, which recently defaulted on three bills of exchange worth $13.5 million, owes a further 7.018 billion baht ($270 million) in bonds and loans to 38 financial institutions, according to company data.
The firm, which played roles in some of the biggest deals in Thai financial circles over the last six years, has more short-term debts that are due for payment soon.
"We have to solve the liquidity problem first and then we can discuss long-term planning," said an adviser from Dhana Siam Finance and Securities.
"We haven't talked to the lenders yet, I think we have to talk with them to extend us some kind of credit and we can negotiate after that," he told Reuters.

The plight of One Holding came to light after Finance One Plc, once the largest finance firm in Thailand, had to see off its own liquidity woes by merging with lender Thai Danu Bank Plc earlier this month.

The demise of the expansionist One group mirrored problems experienced by a number of finance firms caught in a stock market that has lost nearly half its value over the past 12 months and a property sector whose speculative bubble has burst.
It also came as the Thai financial sector faced a liquidity and bad loan crisis that forced the authorities to order a revamp of financial institutions earlier this month.
One Holding employs between 200 and 300 staff. Executives, who asked not to be further identified, said talks were now under way to determine how many jobs would have to go.

Because of its financial situation, One Holding has been left out of the Thai Danu merger deal. With Finance One assets frozen pending the merger, assistance from Finance One was highly unlikely, executives said.
"Finance One owns 9.41 percent of One Holding and has leant money to One Holding which is fully collateralised," said a company spokeswoman.
Finance One said earlier this month that One Holding was a debtor with a balance sheet of about 1.0 billion baht in loans and bills of exchange in owings.

One Holding's listing among the "others" section of the exchange meant possible assistance from the central bank's Financial Institutions Rehabilitation Fund, which helps struggling finance firms or banks, was also unlikely, the executives said.
One Holdings could sell assets that include real estate developments with a limited amount of central Bangkok property, shares in small finance companies and some industrials, the executives added.
The value of these will be known following a full assessment of assets early next month, the Dhana Siam adviser said.
If the company survives its current troubles, the prospects are that a rescue plan will return the firm to what it does well -- the rubber business.

"One Holding does three core things," the Dhana Siam adviser said. "It has real estate but the market is not good, it does investment and that is not good either, and it sells rubber and it makes a lot of money from that. If they get through this I think it will go back to rubber," he said.
